Hi Jordan — Rafael from Solutions Engineering here. Quick technical clarifications and an example so your team can map characters -> tokens -> dollars. I’ll keep it practical.

Short answers
1) Characters -> tokens: a rough planning conversion we use is ~4 characters per token for English prose (this is conservative; it varies with punctuation and language). So tokens ≈ characters / 4.

2) What you are billed for: Redwood bills per token processed by the model when it executes (input tokens + output tokens). If a request is served entirely from a server-side cache (we return a cached payload without running the model), you are not billed for model tokens for that request.

3) Prompt/prefix caching vs. KV cache reuse: important differences:
   - Exact-match response caching: if the entire request (prefix + user text) matches a cached response, we can return the cached result and you are not charged token compute for that response. This is the most cost-saving case.
   - Prefix/KV cache reuse: when we reuse KV cache between requests, we still execute the model for the new tokens that differ; billing reflects the tokens that the model actually processes during that run. KV cache reuse reduces latency and compute, but any newly processed tokens (for inputs and outputs) are billed. In short: cache hits that avoid a model run -> no billed tokens; partial reuse that still triggers model computation -> billed for tokens processed.

Example (your numbers)
- Avg user chars: 1,800 -> ~450 input tokens (1,800 / 4)
- Avg generated chars: 700 -> ~175 output tokens
- Tokens per request ≈ 625 (input + output)
- At 1.2M requests/month -> ~750M tokens/month (1.2M * 625)

Cost scenarios (illustrative hosted pricing bands)
- Hosted baseline (example pricing): $30 per 1M tokens -> cost = 750 * $30 = $22,500/month (above your $10k cap).
- Optimized (caching + batching + smaller model for some routes): if we can get 60% of requests served from cache or reduced to 150 tokens avg through summarization/quantization, that could drop to ~300M billed tokens -> $9,000/month at $30/1M (close to your $10k pilot cap).

Recommendations (next actions)
- Run a 2-week sample: we’ll run your CSV through our estimator and identify top-3 routes by token volume to focus caching and summarization.
- Technical deep-dive: Rafael + one infra engineer to look at typical request fingerprints (to estimate realistic cache-hit rate).
- If budget remains a blocker, Dedicated/Reserved capacity with quantized models can materially reduce $/1M tokens; I’ll include a quick back-of-envelope in the MAP.

Notes:
- Requests as a metric are for throughput and SLO planning (RPS, concurrency); billing is tokens-based unless you are returning cached responses that avoid model compute.
- Edge case: if you stream partial results and then stop, billed tokens reflect what the model generated before the stop.

I’ll run the CSV you attached and share two scenarios (hosted vs. dedicated) by end of day Friday.
